scope: Repository benchmark now combines the native streaming scheduler with retained native session pooling, request-sized admission, interleaved CUDA execution, cancellation/refill, and end-to-end arrival-to-fenced-cleanup timing. Execution remains serialized whole-request forward attempts, not multi-request GPU matrix batching.

interface.behavior: runs specifies total jobs (at most100). Source references cycle through request IDs. Prescribed arrivals retain their original monotonic timestamps even when the public64-slot queue has backlog. Cancellation is immediately after the chosen request first successful source prefill, with no generated output. Pool1/live2 exercises acquisition BUSY and serialized progress.
interface.default: Existing blocking/raw-text/sequential-pool/timing paths preserved; no product CLI or library runtime/math change. This is a benchmark adapter using public scheduler callbacks and internal transformer pool APIs, not an HTTP/network service.

ownership.model: Immutable anatomy/weights/config/shared expert and row caches unchanged. Session storage owned by transformer pool, returned once after generation unbinds.
ownership.workspace: Every prepared job has its own scratch/token/piece/recording buffers. Immutable encoder/decoder/prompt owners borrowed from base fixtures; no copying initialized JSON/codec handles. Each job has its own small reference document. All source/codec owners outlive jobs.
ownership.budgets: Separate all3 active quoted payload and retained idle+leased pool payload limits, current and peaks reported. Caller preallocated workspace and recorder payload reported separately. Model/shared caches/codec JSON and tables/control session/metadata/context/allocator overhead separate: not a total physical VRAM/RSS guarantee.

timing.valid: --text-timing: callbacks record clock readings, actual input IDs, token IDs and counted UTF8 bytes only. No callback heap/file IO/logit copies/additional GPU work or fences. Exact source ID/chunk/full-byte verification runs after the timer stops. Separate frozen sourcechecking runs compare every published last F32 vocabulary word.
timing.interval: Model/shared cache setup, immutable codec/source ownership and bounded perjob workspace/recorder initialization outside interval. Arrival backlog, pool acquisition/preparation, raw encoding, scheduler turns, all forward work, cancellation/discard or healthy restart/fences included. Terminal event follows cleanup; metrics are callback availability, not network reception.
timing.output: Perrequest prescribed arrival, admission, first-token, first-byte and terminal timestamps; request/admission/acquire/cleanup intervals, geometry, generated IDs, output hex and history. Summary completed-only nearest-rank p50/p95/p99 with sample counts, window completion/token throughput, all memory budgets and aggregate upload/RAM-miss/source-read counters.
timing.caveats: Sourcecheck mode has timing_valid=false due to reference file IO/F32 copies in callbacks. Capture mode checks IDs/bytes, not every F32 logit in the timed interval. Quantiles from8 completed samples (5 in cancellation case) are descriptive, not statistically qualified production tails. Throughput counts generated output over the entire serving window including prefill/queue/cleanup; it is not isolated decode or prefill throughput.

limits: No multi-request GPU GEMM, kernel preemption or GPU-overlap throughput proof. A long prefill attempt still delays other requests. This measures interleaved logical concurrency.
Synthetic related prompts2050/1026 tokens, five generated tokens, context capacities2304/1280; broader domains, long generations and realistic client arrival distributions still needed.
